skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Reviews changes from a user-supplied Git fixed point along two axes: repository standards and the source spec or issue. It uses parallel subagents to keep the reviews separate, then reports the findings side by side.
skill.summary: Run separated standards and spec reviews for Git changes.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown inline code false positives. The skill does instruct agents to run a setup slash command and Git commands with a user-supplied fixed point, which is a bounded but real external-command risk. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Document what /setup-matt-pocock-skills does, or include the needed issue-tracker setup steps directly in the skill.

remediation.issue: User-supplied Git fixed point in commands
remediation.suggestion: Validate the fixed point before use, reject option-like or shell-control input, and execute Git with argument arrays or strict quoting.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes Against Specs and Standards
content.value_statement: Code reviews often mix style issues with missed requirements. This skill separates standards review from spec review and returns both reports side by side.
actual_capabilities: Compares HEAD with a user-selected commit, branch, tag, or merge base.
Separates review into Standards and Spec axes.
Finds repository standards files such as CODING_STANDARDS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
Uses a fixed Fowler code smell baseline when no stronger repository rule exists.
Runs parallel subagent prompts and aggregates their reports under separate headings.
limitations: It needs a valid fixed point or it must ask the user for one.
It cannot complete the Spec axis when no issue, PRD, or spec source is available.
It depends on repository documentation for project-specific standards.
It reports review findings but does not apply code changes.

use_cases.title: Pre-PR Branch Review
use_cases.description: Review a feature branch before opening a pull request. Catch coding-standard misses and spec gaps separately.

use_cases.title: Team Review Support
use_cases.description: Compare changes against team rules during review. Keep style concerns distinct from requirement concerns.

use_cases.title: Contribution Assessment
use_cases.description: Assess community contributions from a chosen base ref. Identify scope creep and code smells before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Review my current branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-review to review my current branch since main. Separate repository standards findings from spec findings.

prompt_templates.title: Review against a release branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-review on changes since release/2.4. Use the linked issue as the spec source and include the worst finding per axis.

prompt_templates.title: Review a feature with a PRD
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-review since origin/main. Treat docs/prds/import-flow.md as the source spec and include any scope creep.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a long-running branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-review since the merge base with origin/main. Check commit references for issues, apply repository standards, and keep both reports separate.

output: Standards: Two findings, including one possible duplicated validation path.
Spec: One missing acceptance criterion from the linked issue.
Summary: Standards worst issue is duplicated logic; Spec worst issue is the missing error state.

output_examples.input: Review this work against the PRD in docs/prds/search.md.
output: Standards: No documented standard violations found.
Spec: The search filters match the PRD, but the empty-results behavior is missing.
Summary: Standards has zero findings; Spec has one missing behavior.

output_examples.input: Review since HEAD~5 with no available spec.
output: Standards: Reports code smells and repository rule violations from the diff.
Spec: Skipped because no spec source was available.
Summary: Standards findings are reported separately; Spec has no findings to rank.

best_practices: Provide the fixed point and spec source in the first request.
Keep repository standards files current before running the review.
Use the separated reports to assign owners for standards and product gaps.
anti_patterns: Asking for a review without a valid Git reference.
Treating baseline code smells as hard failures when repository standards disagree.
Merging the Standards and Spec reports into one severity list.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Git changes against repository standards and the source spec or issue.

faq.question: Does it change code?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and leaves code edits to the user or another workflow.

faq.question: What fixed point should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a commit, branch, tag, merge base, or another Git ref that marks the comparison point.

faq.question: What happens if there is no spec?
faq.answer: The Spec axis is skipped and the final report states that no spec source was available.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why are there two reports?
faq.answer: Separate reports prevent coding-style issues from masking missed requirements, and prevent requirements issues from masking standards violations.
